Where it began

Steve Smith is a Sydney man, born there on 2 June 1989, and went to Menai High School. As a junior he bowled fast-medium until he was fifteen, then took up leg-spin. At 17 he left school to play in England, where his runs for Sevenoaks Vine in the Kent League earned him games for Surrey's second XI.

He played in the 2008 Under-19 World Cup and first played for New South Wales in January 2008, against Western Australia at the SCG.

The player

Australia first picked him for his leg-spin, and his first Test came at Lord's in July 2010, with him batting down the order. He came back in 2013 as a batter and made his first Test hundred at The Oval at the end of that summer's Ashes, bringing it up with a six. Against India in 2014 and 2015 he made a hundred in every Test of the series, 769 runs at 128.16, and in 2015 he made 215 at Lord's.

By October 2026 he had played 127 Tests and made 11,003 runs at 55.29, with 37 hundreds, 45 fifties and a highest score of 239. He ranks 12th for Test runs and sixth for Test hundreds. He led Australia in 44 Tests, winning 26 of them. His Test batting rating once reached 947, a figure only Don Bradman, on 961, has bettered, and the ICC chose him as the best Test player of the decade from 2011 to 2020.

What made him special

Nobody would teach his method in a coaching manual. Before the ball is bowled there is a shuffle back and across the crease, a move he worked out during an innings at Perth in the 2013-14 Ashes and has kept ever since. After that comes patience: he is happy to bat for hours, and some of his hundreds have been built at little more than a run every three balls.

The leg-spin that first won him a Test cap now appears only now and then: 19 Test wickets at 53.05. It is a reminder of where he started, and a treat for those who are watching when it comes out.

Away from the middle

He was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year in 2016 and has won the Allan Border Medal four times, level with the most ever. He supports the Sydney Roosters in rugby league. Away from Tests he has won titles with the Sydney Sixers, and in 2024 he captained Washington Freedom to the Major League Cricket title, taking the player of the match award in the final.

And finally

By October 2026 he had held more Test catches as a fielder than anyone in the game's history, 224 of them. For a man who arrived as a bowler and stayed as a batter, it seems he was quietly the best fielder in the room as well.
